message: Can you look at this ECG? I think it's normal, right?
reply:
**I wouldn’t call this ECG normal.** The rhythm appears regular, with a heart rate around **60 beats/min**, but there are significant waveform changes:

- Very deep negative complexes in V1–V4, with poor R-wave progression.
- ST elevation in those chest leads, plus ST depression and inverted T waves in I and aVL.

This pattern **suggests left ventricular hypertrophy with “strain”**—electrical changes associated with thickening of the heart’s main pumping chamber. These changes can resemble a heart attack, so the tracing needs clinical context and comparison with previous ECGs. [Clinical reference](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8101826/)

**If you have chest discomfort, breathlessness, sweating, fainting, or new severe symptoms now, call emergency services and don’t drive yourself.** If you feel well, arrange prompt medical review; a repeat ECG, blood-pressure check and potentially an echocardiogram would help clarify this.

Is this your ECG, why was it taken, and are you having any symptoms?
